Predict weight

Source: R/kb_predict_weight.R
kb_predict_weight.Rd

Predict the expected wet weight (kg) of a plant at each row of new_data, or at the observed data when new_data = NULL.

Usage

kb_predict_weight(
  fit,
  new_data = NULL,
  ...,
  new_levels = c("average", "sample"),
  representative_site = NULL,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  estimate = stats::median,
  sig_fig = 3
)

Arguments

fit

A kb_fit_weight object.

new_data

A data frame of the rows to predict at, with the fit's predictor column (diameter_mm or fronds) and optional site and year columns, or NULL for the observed data. year may be numeric or character: 2022 and "2022" match the same fitted year.

...

These dots are for future extensions and must be empty.

new_levels

A string giving how uncertainty is estimated for a site or year not in the data used to fit the model, or when new_data has no site or year column. Sites and years in the model fit always use their own estimates. One of:

  • "average" (the default): the typical site or year. The site and year effects are set to 0, their mean, so the interval does not include among-site or among-year variation. Use it to describe an average site or year.

  • "sample": a new effect for each new site or year, drawn from the estimated variation among sites or among years (the random-effect standard deviation). The point estimate is equivalent, but the interval is wider since it also includes that variation. Use it to get realistic uncertainty about a particular site or year that the model has no information on. Rows that name the same new site or year, or that have no site or year column, share one effect; give new sites or years different names for independent effects. The interval varies slightly between calls; use set.seed() to reproduce it.

representative_site

A character vector of sites in the fit whose effects a new site adopts (averaged when several are named), or NULL (the default) to follow new_levels.

conf_level

A number greater than 0 and less than 1 giving the compatibility-interval level.

estimate

A function that reduces a numeric vector of posterior draws to a single estimate, such as median or mean.

sig_fig

A whole number of significant figures for summary output.

Value

A kb_predictions object: the rows of new_data with added estimate, lower, and upper columns summarising the posterior distribution of expected weight. When the rows have site and year, a weight_support column (as in kb_predict_mean_weight()) precedes the summary.

Details

With representative_site, a new site also takes the named sites' site:year effect in a year in which they have data.

See also

kb_new_data() to build rows by site or year over a predictor sequence, and posterior_predict() for draws of individual plant weights.

Other prediction functions: autoplot.kb_predictions(), kb_new_data(), kb_plot_predictions(), kb_predict_biomass_canopy(), kb_predict_biomass_in_situ(), kb_predict_carbon(), kb_predict_cover_calibration(), kb_predict_mean_weight(), kb_predict_nitrogen(), kb_predict_size(), kb_predict_wetdry(), predict.kb_fit_carbon(), predict.kb_fit_cover_calibration(), predict.kb_fit_nitrogen(), predict.kb_fit_size(), predict.kb_fit_weight(), predict.kb_fit_wetdry()

Examples

fit <- fit_weight_sim_nereo

# At the observed plants:
kb_predict_weight(fit)
#> <kb_predictions> predictor: diameter_mm | response: weight_kg | by: site, year
#> # A tibble: 660 × 8
#>    diameter_mm weight_kg site       year  weight_support estimate lower upper
#>          <dbl>     <dbl> <fct>      <fct> <chr>             <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#>  1        28.6     0.663 otter_cove 2020  site-year         0.779 0.632 0.96 
#>  2        16.5     0.569 otter_cove 2020  site-year         0.262 0.23  0.299
#>  3        27.3     0.841 otter_cove 2020  site-year         0.697 0.567 0.855
#>  4        38.3     1.38  otter_cove 2020  site-year         1.64  1.31  2.08 
#>  5        16.2     0.153 otter_cove 2020  site-year         0.255 0.224 0.291
#>  6        29.8     0.793 otter_cove 2020  site-year         0.861 0.697 1.06 
#>  7        34.7     1.36  otter_cove 2020  site-year         1.27  1.01  1.58 
#>  8        16.2     0.141 otter_cove 2020  site-year         0.255 0.224 0.291
#>  9        25.9     0.311 otter_cove 2020  site-year         0.615 0.505 0.752
#> 10        35.5     1.53  otter_cove 2020  site-year         1.34  1.07  1.68 
#> # ℹ 650 more rows

# Curves by site:
kb_predict_weight(fit, kb_new_data(fit, by = "site"))
#> <kb_predictions> predictor: diameter_mm | response: weight_kg | by: site
#> # A tibble: 180 × 5
#>    site       diameter_mm estimate lower upper
#>    <fct>            <dbl>    <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#>  1 otter_cove        3.8     0.133 0.112 0.158
#>  2 otter_cove        6.12    0.14  0.121 0.163
#>  3 otter_cove        8.45    0.154 0.137 0.176
#>  4 otter_cove       10.8     0.179 0.162 0.2  
#>  5 otter_cove       13.1     0.216 0.195 0.242
#>  6 otter_cove       15.4     0.268 0.239 0.306
#>  7 otter_cove       17.7     0.336 0.296 0.391
#>  8 otter_cove       20.1     0.425 0.367 0.5  
#>  9 otter_cove       22.4     0.535 0.457 0.638
#> 10 otter_cove       24.7     0.671 0.567 0.808
#> # ℹ 170 more rows

# At new measurements:
kb_predict_weight(fit, data.frame(diameter_mm = c(20, 40, 60)))
#> <kb_predictions> predictor: diameter_mm | response: weight_kg
#> # A tibble: 3 × 4
#>   diameter_mm estimate lower  upper
#>         <dbl>    <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl>
#> 1          20    0.434 0.368  0.522
#> 2          40    2.41  1.94   3.08 
#> 3          60    7.58  5.9   10    

# A new site, with between-site variation:
set.seed(1)
kb_predict_weight(
  fit,
  data.frame(diameter_mm = 40, site = "new_site"),
  new_levels = "sample"
)
#> <kb_predictions> predictor: diameter_mm | response: weight_kg | by: site
#> # A tibble: 1 × 5
#>   diameter_mm site     estimate lower upper
#>         <dbl> <chr>       <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1          40 new_site     2.45  1.16  5.26
